activity.notes: Guru Nanak is the historical founder and first Guru of Sikhism. Reference works place his transformative religious experience at Sultanpur probably around 1499, after which he began his preaching mission. ATLAS records c.1499 as a representative person-specific religious-activity point within the Delhi Sultanate rather than fabricating a continuous single-polity rail across his later wide travels and the 1526 transition to Mughal rule.

sources.title: Nanak, Guru — Encyclopedia of Religion / Encyclopedia.com
sources.citation_text: The reference identifies Guru Nanak (1469–1539) as the founder of the Sikh religion and states that at Sultanpur, probably in 1499, he experienced God's call and then began his religious mission.

sources.title: Sikh Philosophy — Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
sources.citation_text: The Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy identifies Guru Nanak as the founder of the Sikh spiritual path and places the emergence of Sikh philosophy in the fifteenth century from his writings and teaching.
